title: DRAM retail price per GB (nominal), 1990-2024: annual series, AI Impacts' published rates, and our nominal fits

units.usd_per_gb_2020usd: US$ per GB in 2020 dollars (CPI-adjusted by AI Impacts)

conventions: Series = annual geometric mean of McCallum's dated retail price points (his '$/Mbyte' column x1000 = $/GB), calendar year = floor(date); 1990-2017 from the AI Impacts spreadsheet copy, 2018-2024 from a 2024 Wayback capture of McCallum's table (single extraction; 2024 partial year). Plot on log y, linear x. McCallum's data are retail/street prices of memory modules, not DRAM contract or spot prices. Two kinds of rate: 'fits' = AI Impacts' published rates (2020 dollars; the -36/-33 values are whole-series averages, the -15/-12 values are 'from 2010 onwards'); 'our_nominal_fits' = our OLS fits to the plotted nominal annual series (what the s09 chart draws).

mccallum_via_aiimpacts.cite: John C. McCallum, 'Historical Memory Prices 1957+' (jcmit.net/memoryprice.htm), as copied in the AI Impacts spreadsheet, tab 'McCallum Data' (nominal $/GB = col C; 2020$ = col D)

aiimpacts2020.cite: Asya Bergal, 'Trends in DRAM price per gigabyte', AI Impacts, 2020

mccallum_wayback.cite: J. C. McCallum, Memory Prices (Wayback capture 2024)

cross_check.unc: derived: OLS slope of ln($/GB) vs date over raw points, rate = exp(slope)-1; irregular sampling, not time-weighted
cross_check.note: post-2010 matches AI Impacts (-15). Pre-2010 over 1990-2010 gives about -40 vs published -36 (AI Impacts fit window not stated). Deck uses the published -36.

extraction.agent_b: independent blind extraction (dram_price_trend.b.json; McCallum via Wayback, 1990-2024)
extraction.method: Table values (no chart read). jcmit.net/memoryprice.htm is not retrievable: the live domain currently serves an unrelated Swedish casino page (saved text discarded); Wayback snapshot (20250718164932) returned HTTP 429 on repeated tries. The same McCallum table was taken from the AI Impacts spreadsheet. Annual values are geometric means (our aggregation).

cross_check.resolved: A (AI Impacts sheet, nominal + 2020$) used for 1990-2017; B nominal values appended for 2018-2024 (single extraction). Published fits are CPI-adjusted (2020$); plotted series is nominal -> caption must say so. Neither includes the 2025-26 spike.

extraction.metadata_revision: 2026-10-04 (report review R2): title, conventions, fit labels and series-end caveat updated to match the data; values unchanged.

caveats: Series covers 1990-2024: 1990-2017 from the AI Impacts copy (last point 2017.92), 2018-2024 from the Wayback capture (single extraction, 2024 partial year). Nothing covers the 2025-26 price spike; do not extend the line.

McCallum prices are retail module prices (mostly Newegg-type listings after 2005), not DRAM contract prices; annual means over 4-12 irregular points, so single-year bumps (e.g. 2010, 2013, 2017) are partly sampling noise.
Values come via AI Impacts' spreadsheet copy, not directly from jcmit.net; footer should say 'McCallum data via AI Impacts'. Tag [S] as approved by Kamil.
Series is nominal $/GB; AI Impacts fits use 2020 dollars. Both given; nominal and 2020$ post-2010 slopes both near -15%.
Fits are the two datasets' published rates; the Objective Analysis series itself is not included (no numbers beyond the graph digitisation). Our own nominal fits are in our_nominal_fits.
Break at 2010-2011 matches Handy (thememoryguy.com 2019-11-20) '2011 or so' (via notes/q3 section 1, not re-fetched).
Fallback not needed (series_available true), but fits alone suffice for the fallback panel.

our_nominal_fits.method: OLS of ln($/GB) on year, rate = exp(slope)-1
OLS of ln($/GB) on year, rate = exp(slope)-1
our_nominal_fits.note: sensitive to break year: 2011-2024 gives about -10, 2010-2017 about -13
